description: The Interaction & Events block-heads `when`/`every`/`on_key`/`on_click` declared as procedures with Core Language alone: all four raise `ol-reserved-word`. This is the byte-identical source its twin `block-heads-reserved-under-profile` runs with the profile ACTIVE, and after issue #841 the two fixtures expect the same four diagnostics -- which is precisely what `spec/grammar.md:408` requires: "a program cannot declare which profiles it requires ... so a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner". The pair's job has inverted with it. It used to prove the reservation was profile-SCOPED; it now proves the reservation does NOT vary with the profile set, and it still takes both fixtures to say so -- either one alone is satisfied by an implementation that answers the same way for the wrong reason. HISTORY, and why the file name is now false: issue #688 wrote this to pin the `ONLY within` half of `spec/interaction-events.md:43-47` ("An implementation that does not declare this profile does not reserve those words..."), expecting zero diagnostics. Ruling #833 retracted that half, issue #855 removed the sentence from the spec, and #841 removed the gate from the checker. Nothing here is "free core only" any more. Inverted rather than deleted so the regression lock survives the reversal with its history attached; renaming belongs to issue #842's corpus sweep. `"check": true`: static legality only, nothing executes. `message` is deliberately absent from the diagnostics below, and the asymmetry with the twin is intentional rather than an oversight: the harness does not compare `message` even when a fixture supplies it (measured -- a deliberately wrong `message` here still passed the suite), so including it would add an assertion nothing verifies. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and "prose is presentation" (`spec/error-model.md:253`); the learner-facing wording is pinned by unit tests instead. Dropping the decorative `message` from the twins is a corpus-wide edit and belongs to issue #842.
